title: Two classes of knots and the global hollow triples
claim: If the knots of a finite pattern split into two classes with equal pair counts, the two classes and their union have the same NAE states; so each knot of one class is forced by the other. Registered on OVERLAP-READ's 98 global swap-made bases: G1 (every global hollow triple a removed source knot) held on 91 and failed on 7; G2 (the untouched class forces each removed knot, 85 bases) held.
failure_conditions: A six-regular one-pair weave whose two classes have different states.
A global hollow triple of OVERLAP-READ's 98 bases that is not a removed source knot.
A removed knot not forced by the untouched class.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite knot patterns under NAE; the registered check on OVERLAP-READ's swap-made bases.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's go-ahead on 2026-11-11; read by an independent referee (a fresh agent with its own code), which found the lemma and check.py correct, asked for the equal-pair-count statement (made) and characterized G1's exceptions.
validation.status: proved by hand; check.py ran as registered: C1 and G2 passed, G1 failed on 7 of 98 (a registered prediction, not the lemma); refereed
validation.novelty: known-with-delta: an instance of trades and of the NAE-to-max-cut gadget; the reading of the swap-made bases' global hollow triples is the delta.
